title: Pre-flight & Tooling (v0.64.0)
description: Soup CLI v0.64.0 pre-flight & tooling — catch mistakes before you burn GPU hours. soup tunability ranks candidate bases for the Pareto frontier (a deterministic heuristic by default, --live to probe each one). soup plan/apply is Terraform-shaped drift detection. soup env lock snapshots the Python version, the CUDA version when it can find one, and the installed ones among 15 tracked packages, with ABI-mismatch detection. soup completions for bash/zsh/fish. soup license-advisor returns ok/warn/block per deploy target. Hardware-fit calculator predicts peak VRAM in 5 buckets with 10% safety margin.

Pre-flight & Tooling (v0.64.0)

Six surfaces that catch mistakes before you spend a GPU hour: pick the right base, lock the run plan, freeze the environment, install completions, advise on licenses, and predict peak VRAM.

soup tunability — Pareto frontier of base-model efficiency

Ranks candidate bases by how much fine-tuning is likely to buy on your data, and reports which of them form the Pareto frontier (best efficiency for cost). By default the score is a deterministic heuristic, not a measurement. Add --live (with --device) to actually probe each candidate with a lightweight LoRA on a held-out slice and rank on measured training-loss deltas.

--candidates is an allowlist, and a name outside it exits non-zero rather than falling back. The eight bundled candidates are qwen3-0.6b, qwen3-1.7b, llama-3.2-1b, llama-3.2-3b, gemma-3-e2b, phi-4-mini, smollm3-1.7b and qwen2.5-1.5b; --list prints them with their licences, and --plan-only dry-runs without probing.

  • Candidate allowlist with licensing metadata (Apache-2.0 / MIT / LLaMA-3 / etc.)
  • Bounds: probe_steps ∈ [10, 10000], holdout_size ∈ [10, 100000] rows
  • Safety: path containment, null-byte rejection, symlink-escape rejection
  • Output: per-candidate delta, wall-clock seconds, estimated USD cost, Pareto membership

soup plan / soup apply — Terraform-shaped drift detection

blocks.code:
soup plan --config soup.yaml --state ./soup.tfstate
soup apply --config soup.yaml --state ./soup.tfstate

blocks.html:
plan computes cost / ETA / peak-VRAM / SHA-256 hashes from the config and writes an immutable soup.tfstate. apply re-reads the config, detects any drift (batch size, dataset SHA, base SHA) and refuses to proceed (exit 3) until you re-plan. apply does not start training: with no drift it marks the plan applied in the state file and prints the soup train --config ... command to run.

Since v0.76.0 both commands run the same unknown-key check as soup train: a config with a key the schema does not know is refused with unknown config key 'x' - refused. and exit 1. At v0.75.x they skipped it, so a plan could be written, and applied, for a config soup train would then reject. Apart from the YAML read limits below, that is the only check they run: they read the YAML as a plain mapping and do not run the schema validation that soup train does. Checked at v0.76.0: soup plan writes a plan for a config that sets training.quantization_aware: true, which soup doctor --config and soup train refuse at load. Checked again at v0.77.0, which refuses more at load: soup plan still writes a plan (exit 0) for a config that sets a staged field away from its default, one that soup train refuses with exit 1. Run soup doctor --config soup.yaml first (see the settings refused at load). Since v0.76.1 both commands read the file under the shared YAML limits: a config larger than 1 MiB, nested more than 100 levels deep or expanding past its alias allowance exits 2 with one line such as config 'soup.yaml' is larger than 1048576 bytes; refusing (v0.76.0 read such a file, and plan wrote a plan for it). A YAML syntax error still exits 1 (see Size and nesting limits).

  • Pure JSON state: plan{cost, eta, sha}, applied: bool, applied_at, run_id
  • TOCTOU defense: os.lstat before open, symlinks rejected
  • Peak VRAM with 10% safety margin; spot pricing per GPU tier
  • Composes with v0.67 soup lock for full reproducibility

soup env lock / status / check — hermetic environment

blocks.code:
soup env lock --output ./soup-env.lock
soup env check --lock ./soup-env.lock   # exit 3 on ABI drift
soup env check                          # v0.73.3: also audits declared bounds, no lock needed

blocks.html:
Snapshots the Python version, the platform, the CUDA version and, for each of 15 ABI-sensitive packages that is installed, its version (torch, transformers, peft, trl, accelerate, datasets, bitsandbytes, huggingface-hub, flash-attn, xformers, deepspeed, unsloth, vllm, sentencepiece, tokenizers) into a JSON lockfile; a tracked package that is not installed is left out. check flags drift in any of them (a Python minor version, the platform, any change of the recorded CUDA version string, a tracked package whose version changed or that appeared or disappeared) that would silently break training. The CUDA version is read from the CUDA_VERSION or CUDA_HOME environment variable, or from PyTorch only if it is already imported; without the variables no CUDA version is recorded, so a CUDA change goes unseen.

Since v0.73.3 it also audits your installed packages against Soup's own declared version bounds, and exits 3 when one is violated. That runs first and independently of any lock file, so it catches the case it was reported for: installing a fast serving stack into a training environment silently pushes transformers past the upper bound Soup itself declares (<5.0.0 when this check shipped in v0.73.3, <6.0.0 since the v0.74 stack move), producing an environment Soup's own metadata calls unsupported with no warning at any point. The bounds are read from package metadata rather than a second hardcoded copy, because a second copy is exactly the drift this is meant to catch. The lock diagnostic still prints either way, so a bounds violation cannot hide a missing lock file or an ABI drift.

The practical guidance that came with it: install [serve-fast] in a separate environment from [train]. Their resolutions are genuinely incompatible today.

soup env fix — the repair, once check has told you something is wrong

blocks.code:
soup env fix                                   # print a uv-pip install plan from the lock
soup env fix --format requirements             # print it as requirements lines instead
soup env fix --format requirements -o req.txt  # also write that file, under cwd

blocks.html:
It renders a reproducible install plan from soup-env.lock and prints it. It never installs anything, and that is deliberate rather than unfinished: recreating a virtual environment is environment-dependent, so Soup emits the commands for you to read, paste or script rather than shelling out to a package manager on your behalf. With no lock file it exits 1 and tells you to run soup env lock first.

  • Fields: soup_version, python_version, platform, cuda_version, packages {name, version, source}
  • Atomic write, file-size capped
  • Feeds the env_hash half of v0.67 soup.lock closure

soup completions <shell> — bash / zsh / fish

blocks.code:
soup completions bash  | sudo tee /etc/bash_completion.d/soup
soup completions zsh   > ~/.zsh/completions/_soup
soup completions fish  > ~/.config/fish/completions/soup.fish

blocks.html:
Eval-safe shell completion scripts emitted to stdout (no Rich panels). Closed shell allowlist; all error messages go to stderr. They complete command and option names only: no option or argument has a value completer, so recipe names, config keys and file values do not complete.

soup license-advisor — deploy-target risk gate

Returns ok / warn / block (exit 3 on block) for a (license, deploy-target, MAU) tuple. Targets: b2c, defense, embedded — each with distinct rules. Composes with v0.60 license-matrix on soup adapters merge.

Hardware-fit calculator — analytical peak VRAM

blocks.code:
from soup_cli.utils.hardware_fit import HardwareFitInput, decide_hardware_fit

report = decide_hardware_fit(
    HardwareFitInput(
        params_b=8.0, seq_len=2048, batch_size=1,
        optimizer="adamw_torch", quant="4bit", peft="qlora",
        gradient_checkpointing=True,
    ),
    available_vram_gb=24.0,
)
# report.ok, report.peak_vram_gb, report.required_with_margin_gb, report.reason
# report.breakdown.weights_gb, .optimizer_gb, .gradients_gb, .activations_gb, .overhead_gb

blocks.html:
estimate_peak_vram_gb(HardwareFitInput(...)) returns just the five-field VRAMBreakdown (in GB). Both are predictions from a static formula, not measurements.

Static predictor with a 5-bucket breakdown (weights / optimizer / gradients / activations / overhead) and a 10% safety margin. Refuses to run if predicted peak exceeds available VRAM.

If you disagree with it, soup train --allow-oom-attempt bypasses this gate and launches anyway. It is opt-out rather than opt-in for a reason: a prediction that refuses a run which would have worked costs you an argument, while a run that launches and does not fit costs you the run. Note this is the analytical gate for an ordinary resident run. Layer streaming skips it entirely and uses its own budget instead, which this flag does not reach; the streaming equivalents are the config keys stream_vram_probe and stream_vram_override.

  • 9 quant tiers (none, 4bit, 8bit, fp8, gptq, awq, aqlm, eetq, mxfp4). Since v0.76.0 soup train runs the gate for all nine; through v0.75.2 the CLI checked only none, 4bit and 8bit (mxfp4 joined in v0.76.0 with the other five, #1631, #1652). fp8 is priced at 2.0 bytes per parameter (it was 1.0), because an FP8 base is dequantized on load and trains in bf16, and a refusal for it adds An FP8 base is dequantized on load, so this estimate prices the bf16 model. An hqq:* value has no memory model yet, so the run starts and prints Pre-flight skipped: no memory model for quantization: hqq:4bit instead of staying silent. A config in one of the six newly checked formats that used to start on a card too small for the estimate is now refused; --allow-oom-attempt launches it anyway. No measured error is published for these formats.
  • 4 PEFT modes (full, lora, dora, qlora)
  • Where soup train gets the model size: a local checkpoint is measured from its safetensors headers (since v0.77.0 the checkpoint's own files: the ones model.safetensors.index.json names, else model.safetensors, else the model-*-of-*.safetensors shards, else every *.safetensors except consolidated*. A consolidated.safetensors beside them, the mistral-inference copy Mistral's repositories ship, is no longer counted, and the same rule applies to soup profile and soup cost, #1806, #1906); a Hub id is sized from its name (72B, 8x7B read as 46.7B total, an active-parameter marker such as -A22B ignored, 135M as 0.135B). A name with no size token is sized as 7B, so the gate can pass a run that will not fit: point base: at a local download to have it measured.
  • Bounds: seq_len ∈ [64, 1M], batch ∈ [1, 1024], params ∈ (0, 1000B]
  • Activation memory halved under gradient checkpointing

soup doctor and soup bench train

Two more checks that run before a GPU hour sit on the Fine-tune Doctor page: soup doctor --config soup.yaml (which settings your config switches on that its backend never reads, and the load refusals of v0.76.0 and v0.77.0, staged fields included) and soup bench train (a short run that fails when the model was not training). soup doctor itself, on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, also reports each card's compute capability and architecture family (Blackwell, Hopper, Ada, Ampere, Turing, Volta, Pascal), says when the installed PyTorch build has no native or PTX support for it and prints a CUDA-matched reinstall hint, and lists BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 hardware and software support in a Precision features block. That GPU panel was read from the code at v0.76.0 and not run here.

Numbers

Six surfaces, +N tests on top of v0.63's 10,035. Composes downstream with v0.65 eval depth, v0.66 post-train x-rays, and v0.67 adapter lifecycle.
